name: tma_oob
kind: attribution: does the out-of-bounds part of a TMA tile load use the memory path; no workload-based fitting
question: A TMA tile load whose box lies partly or wholly outside the tensor's global_dim returns fill values for the out-of-bounds elements. Does that part of the box still cost L2 read requests, crossbar delivery to the SM and completion time like an in-bounds part of the same size, alone and when every SM loads at once?
motivation: fg-over20 notes 2026-11-13 (tools/tmacmp.py): in full-gpu cases whose TMA boxes overhang the tensor (flashinfer segment GEMM, CuTe-DSL / flashinfer block-scaled GEMM, cutlass sparse) the converter's access rows hold only the in-bounds sectors (16-63 % of the box bytes; several UTMALDG PCs have none), while the hardware counters show l1tex__m_xbar2l1tex_read_sectors x 32 B equal to the full box bytes (FIF-BS-SM103-NVF4-C03: 127.8 MB delivered, 21.3 MB in bounds; flashinfer_segment_01: 100.8 against 21.0) and lts__t_sectors_srcunit_tex_op_read near the full box bytes. Consumer warps of these cases wait for TMA data 10-30 points of warp time longer on hardware than in the engine. The engine gives out-of-bounds sectors no memory path (python/cyclescope/convert/tensor_map.py tiled_box_rectangle; engine: the completion leaf plus the hierarchy's waits of the in-bounds sectors only).
probe: tma_oob.cu = tma_loaded.cu (same kernel body, same 64 x 128 bf16 SWIZZLE_128B box of 16 KiB, one warp per slot, issue -> test_wait spin -> re-issue, global arrival counter) with one added axis: the x coordinate of every load. The tensor is 64 bf16 wide (128 B rows); x = 0 loads in-bounds boxes, x = 32 loads boxes whose rows are half outside (8 KiB in bounds), x = 64 loads boxes entirely outside. y walks the CTA's own region exactly as in tma_loaded (hot mode: 24 MiB tensor resident in L2 after the discarded first launch). Cells: N in {1, 16, all SMs} x S in {1, 4, 8} x x in {0, 32, 64}; runs a and b, 8 samples, 2048 rounds. Counters: the N = all, S = 4 cells of each x once more under ncu (--cache-control none for this pass only, the question is traffic not cold latency) with dram__bytes_read.sum, lts__t_sectors_srcunit_tex_op_read.sum (+ lookup_hit / lookup_miss), l1tex__m_xbar2l1tex_read_sectors.sum, sm__cycles_active.max.

controls.sass: one UTMALDG.2D per round in the timed loop of k_tma_oob; the three x values use the same kernel (x is a run-time argument).
controls.data: after the last round the host-visible check: thread 0 of CTA 0 sums the first 64 B of its slot-0 box into the output record; x = 64 must read all zeros (fill), x = 0 the memset pattern. A wrong sum fails the cell.
controls.timing: x = 0 cells reproduce tma_loaded (hot) of the same device within 10 % on latency p50 and aggregate bytes per ns; runs a and b agree within 10 %.

derivation: Per cell: latency p50 (issue -> complete), per-CTA box rate (boxes per 1000 cycles), aggregate boxes per ns; ratios x = 32 / x = 0 and x = 64 / x = 0. Counter pass: xbar read sectors per box and L2 tex read sectors per box for each x.

predictions_before_data.traffic: xbar read sectors per box = 512 (the whole 16 KiB box) for x = 0, 32 and 64 alike (within 5 %); L2 tex read sectors per box within 25 % of 512 for all three; DRAM bytes per box about 0 in the hot mode for all three.
predictions_before_data.time: latency p50 and box rate of x = 32 and x = 64 within 15 % of x = 0 in every (N, S) cell: an out-of-bounds box is as slow as an in-bounds one, also when all SMs load 4-8 boxes at once.
predictions_before_data.engine_today: the engine as it stands predicts x = 64 at the unloaded completion leaf for every N and S (no shared waits), i.e. faster than x = 0 under load by the amount x = 0 slows down from N = 1 to N = all.

outcomes_before_data.same: If traffic and time predictions hold: rule = the out-of-bounds part of a tiled TMA load issues L2 read requests for (box bytes - in-bounds bytes) / 32 sectors which are served as L2 hits (no residency state, no DRAM) through the same per-GPC and device read services and the same SM delivery as in-bounds sectors; the engine derives the count from the access's transfer_bytes and its sector rows. No new leaf value.
outcomes_before_data.cheaper: If out-of-bounds boxes are faster by more than 15 % under load but still show full xbar traffic: report the ratio per (N, S); a rule needs a second experiment separating L2 lookup from delivery; nothing installed.
outcomes_before_data.free: If out-of-bounds boxes show no L2 / xbar traffic in this probe: the full-gpu counter reading has another cause (to be found); nothing installed.

prediction_check: Replay of the x = 0 and x = 64 cells (N = all, S = 4) through tracer -> convert -> engine with the rule: simulated box rate within 15 % of hardware for both; then the full-gpu 500 x 2 regression.
not_allowed: No family / case / shape specific timing, no tuning to the full-gpu error. Any post-data change of a criterion is labelled with its reason.

addenda.runs: $CYCLESCOPE_ARTIFACT_ROOT/microbench/tma_oob/{h100-r3,b300-r1}; h100-r1 / r2 are failed build rounds). SASS: the timed loop is unrolled by ptxas into 5 UTMALDG (as in tma_loaded), the gate was changed to 5 before the run that counts.
addenda.text: Traffic prediction held for the crossbar only: l1tex__m_xbar2l1tex_read_sectors per box = 512 for x = 0 / 32 / 64 on both devices (the whole box is delivered to the SM whatever is in bounds); L2 tex read sectors per box = 512 / 320-343 / 133-153 (not the predicted ~512 for all). Time prediction (out-of-bounds within 15 % of in-bounds) FAILED in both directions. (1) A box entirely outside (x = 64) alone costs what an in-bounds box costs (latency p50 615 / 602 cycles h100 / b300, box rate equal at N = 1 and 16 for S = 1 on both; h100 N = 16, S = 4 / 8 already 16-24 % slower); with every SM loading, b300 does not slow it down (5.26 / 6.46 boxes per 1000 cycles and CTA at S = 4 / 8 against 4.10 / 4.15 in bounds), h100 slows it MORE than in-bounds (0.93 / 1.19 / 1.54 at S = 1 / 4 / 8 against 1.32 / 1.76 / 1.79). (2) A box half outside along dimension 0 (x = 32, every row half in bounds) is a different regime on both devices: latency +166 / +178 cycles alone (781 / 780), and the SM delivers at most 3.87-3.89 such boxes per 1000 cycles whatever S (4 or 8) and N (1, 16, all) — 258 cycles of per-SM serial service per 16-KiB box; in-bounds boxes reach 6.46 / 7.63 at N = 1, S = 8. Runs a and b agree to the printed digits. Outcome per the protocol: none of the three declared outcomes as written (not 'same', not 'cheaper', not 'free'); nothing is installed from v1. What the engine does today: an out-of-bounds part has no sectors, the completion leaf is taken at transfer_bytes = full box, service starts serialize at storage.async.service_start — so x = 64 alone is right by construction, x = 32 is too fast (no +170, no 258-cycle serial service), and the full-card h100 slowdown of x = 64 is absent. Protocol v2 (protocol-v2.json) asks for the functional form: overhang fraction, overhang along dimension 1 (whole rows outside), box size.
